authority.legal_name: State of Hawaiʻi Department of Transportation, Harbors Division (public inter-island harbors mandate), with Pulama Lānaʻi as the launch anchor operator on Lānaʻi
authority.geography_type: an isolated archipelago of six main islands separated by deep, open ocean channels of widely varying exposure

mandate.summary: Hawaiʻi DOT Harbors Division operates the State's commercial and passenger harbor system across all major islands. Hawaiʻi has had no scheduled statewide inter-island ferry since the Superferry ceased in 2009, leaving inter-island travel almost entirely dependent on aviation. The mandate is safe, reliable inter-island mobility consistent with the State's environmental law and its statutory decarbonization goals.
current_priorities: Restoring viable inter-island passenger mobility without repeating the Superferry's wake / whale-strike / environmental-review failure
Advancing Hawaiʻi's statutory clean-transportation and carbon-neutrality goals across the harbor system
Reducing dependence on inter-island aviation and Oʻahu road congestion

policy_targets.interim_target: 100% renewable electricity by 2045 (statutory RPS) and statewide carbon neutrality by 2045 (Act 15, 2018)
policy_targets.vision: Hawaiʻi Clean Energy Initiative and the State's 2045 carbon-neutral / 100%-renewable law — a whole-economy decarbonization that a zero-emission marine mode advances directly
policy_targets.relevance: A zero-emission, low-wake foiling inter-island service advances the 2045 carbon-neutral goal while restoring a public mobility mode Hawaiʻi has lacked for over a decade — and does it in the one way the 2009 environmental review demanded: without damaging wake or whale-strike risk.

precedent.headline: Hawaiʻi already runs an inter-island passenger ferry — and already proved the latent statewide demand.

existing_ferry.route: Lahaina / Māʻalaea (Maui) ↔ Manele Harbor (Lānaʻi) across the ʻAuʻau Channel
existing_ferry.service: Daily scheduled passenger service, expanded to three round trips per day (2024); ~45–60 minute crossing
existing_ferry.proof_stat: A continuously operating, sheltered-channel inter-island passenger ferry — the live proof that scheduled inter-island service works in Hawaiʻi.
existing_ferry.note: Pulama Lānaʻi stewards ~98% of Lānaʻi and Four Seasons Lānaʻi; the Maui–Lānaʻi crossing is the natural launch anchor.

superferry_lesson.stat: Carried 300,000+ passengers in under two years before an environmental-review ruling shut it down
superferry_lesson.relevance: Proves deep latent statewide demand AND defines the bar: the wake and whale-strike concerns that grounded a large diesel fast-cat are exactly what a foiling, low-wake, zero-emission hull answers.

interpretation_for_navier: Hawaiʻi is not an untested market. A sheltered-channel inter-island ferry already runs (Maui–Lānaʻi), and the Superferry already proved 300k+ passengers of latent statewide demand. What is missing is a vessel that clears the exact bar the 2009 review set — low-wake, quiet, whale-safe, zero-emission. A foiling hull that flies clear of the water is that vessel. Lead with the live Maui–Lānaʻi crossing, then reconnect the main islands.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat]. Precise berths and routed geometry are Grok's to seal. Coordinates are anchor-grade.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The live Expeditions crossing across the sheltered ʻAuʻau Channel — the launch anchor. Foiling makes today's ferry faster, quieter and zero-emission.
The alternate Maui harbor to Lānaʻi; extends the anchor crossing to Māʻalaea's central Maui catchment.
Oʻahu to Molokaʻi across the Kaʻiwi Channel — reconnects an underserved community island to Honolulu; Quanta-LR hybrid, no outer-harbor charging needed.
Oʻahu to Maui line-haul — the core statewide corridor the Superferry served; the latent-demand backbone.
Maui to Molokaʻi across the Pailolo Channel — short inter-island connector within Maui County.
Maui to Hawaiʻi Island across the ʻAlenuihāhā Channel — among the roughest channels on Earth; a foiling hull that cancels the chop turns the worst crossing in Hawaiʻi into the smoothest.
Oʻahu to Kauaʻi across the Kaʻieʻie/Kauaʻi Channel — the Garden Isle line-haul; longest-exposure leg, Quanta-LR.

regional_links.note: Hawaiʻi is an isolated archipelago with no adjacent jurisdiction; there is no cross-border regional link. The 'reach' dimension is instead the longest, roughest open-ocean channels, all domestic.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every leg is an open-ocean channel crossing between islands; route each through open navigable water only, with explicit hand waypoints clear of reefs, headlands and the humpback sanctuary. No leg may cross island land.

hazards.hazard: Hawaiian Islands Humpback Whale National Marine Sanctuary
hazards.detail: Federally protected humpback habitat, peak season roughly November–May, concentrated in the ʻAuʻau / Pailolo / Maui-County waters. This is the defining constraint that ended the Superferry. Low-wake foiling and seasonal speed/route discipline are mandatory; document whale-safe routing explicitly.
The Maui–Hawaiʻi Island channel (haw-d06) is among the roughest on Earth with extreme wind acceleration off Haleakalā and Mauna Kea. Route and schedule with weather-aware waypoints.
Open, deep, trade-wind-exposed crossings (haw-d03, haw-d07); mid-channel routing clear of Oʻahu's eastern and western headlands.
Manele, Kaunakakai, Kawaihae and Nāwiliwili have reef-fringed approaches; route to charted harbor entrances, never straight-line to shore.
Honolulu is a busy commercial port; departures must follow the charted entrance channel and traffic scheme.
